newsitem.title: FRANCE: AGF's CDE sees loss narrowing in 1996.
newsitem.headline: AGF's CDE sees loss narrowing in 1996.

text.p: Property lender Comptoir des Entrepreneurs (CDE) expects to report a loss of less than 100 million francs for 1996, chairman Jacques Lebhar said in an interview published on Thursday in newspaper Les Echos.

"We expect to show a loss inferior to 100 million francs," he said. CDE, 77-percent owned by insurance company Assurances Generales de France (AGF), had a net attributable loss of 560.4 million francs in 1995 after losing 1.02 billion in 1994.
Lebhar said asset sales should reach 500 million francs by year's end. He also said he believed AGF had dropped its search for a buyer for part of its stake in CDE.
